notes.short-video: Reviewed the five largest rating counts: Picsart, Likee, ReelShort, PineDrama and Clapper. Likee and Clapper describe social video; Picsart is an editing tool and looks wrong for a consumption block. ReelShort and PineDrama are scripted microdramas, a policy boundary if this means social clips only. Known recall failure: the separate bundle lookup found TikTok, but this keyword search did not. Listing metadata only, no apps played.
notes.dating: Reviewed Plenty of Fish, Bumble, Tinder, Hinge and BLK. All five descriptions explicitly offer dating; no obvious mismatch in this sample. Both Lifestyle and Social Networking appear, so one genre filter would miss plausible members. This selected high-rating-count sample does not establish precision for the rest of the queue.
notes.betting: Reviewed FanDuel, DraftKings, Kalshi, PrizePicks and Hard Rock Bet. Four describe betting or cash picks and return Gambling advisories. Kalshi describes regulated prediction-market event trading, is in Finance and returns no advisories. Its inclusion is a policy decision for financial speculation, not something the Sports genre or gambling descriptor can settle. This is not a legal classification or a product-use test.
notes.social: Reviewed Facebook, WhatsApp, Messenger, Discord and Life360. Facebook clearly describes feed/video consumption. WhatsApp and Messenger are messaging services; Discord describes group chat and communities; Life360 is family safety and location tracking. Life360 looks wrong, and messaging/group chat are poor fits if the category means public social feeds. These chart/search seeds require much stricter human review.
notes.news: Reviewed Apple News, CNN, NewsBreak, SmartNews and NYTimes. All five describe journalism or news aggregation; no obvious mismatch for a broad News block. Their descriptors do not identify doomscrolling, and this sample does not prove that every remaining search result is a news publisher.
notes.shopping: Reviewed Walmart, Amazon Shopping, Etsy, Target and SHEIN. All five describe purchasing goods; no obvious mismatch for broad Shopping. Walmart and Target also cover groceries and essentials, which may be too broad for a discretionary-shopping block. Rating count cannot make that distinction.
notes.loot-boxes: Reviewed Roblox, Toca Boca World, Magic Sort!, Fortnite and ibis Paint X. Roblox, Magic Sort! and Fortnite explicitly return Loot Boxes. ibis Paint X is an illustration tool and looks wrong. Toca Boca World describes open-ended creative play and has no returned advisory, so it is unsupported for this category. Gacha keyword results must not become an automatic block list. Explicit descriptors are listing claims, not a fresh gameplay audit.
notes.casino: Reviewed Quick Hit Casino, Gold Fish Casino, Classic Slots, Jackpot World and myKONAMI. All five describe slots/social-casino play and return Frequent/Intense Simulated Gambling. No obvious mismatch for a broad simulated-casino queue in this sample. The descriptors and promotional descriptions do not prove every monetization, cash-out or sweepstakes detail.
